lockup.summary: The company agreed not to sell new shares for 180 days. Directors, executives and holders of 10% or more cannot sell for 12 months. Other existing shareholders cannot sell for 6 months. The lead underwriter can give written permission to sell earlier.

what: It owns and runs 24 nursery centers in the United Kingdom, caring for children from three months to five years old.
proceeds: It plans to use the money, plus its existing cash, mainly to pay for the Grolife acquisition (about £6.2 million up front and £1.7 million later) and the Bright Eyes acquisition (about £1.5 million). The rest goes to legal costs and general business needs.
risks: It has grown fast and may struggle to manage that growth at its current size.
It has little experience in specialist education, and there is no guarantee it will succeed there.
It has lost money from operations in the past and may not stay profitable.
It may fail to find good acquisitions, or to combine them into its business, which could slow its growth.
